item.title: Principal Adviser, Parliamentary Strengthening, Brussels
item.description: Context The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA) is an intergovernmental organisation dedicated to promoting sustainable democracy worldwide. Its mission is to strengthen democratic institutions and processes. The Institute serves as a catalyst for democracy building by offering global comparative knowledge, resources, tools and policy proposals, and by supporting democratic reforms in response to specific national requests. Its areas of work encompass democracy assessment and strategic foresight, electoral processes, constitutional governance and rule of law, political participation and representation, including parliamentary strengthening and money in politics, as well as democratic resilience and the intersection of democracy with gender and inclusion, climate change, technology, including AI, and security. Global Programmes implements International IDEA’s institutional areas of work and develops global comparative knowledge, approaches and tools to support democratic institutions and processes. It works closely with Regional and Country Programmes to support the application of global knowledge and expertise in different contexts. Parliamentary strengthening is a core component of International IDEA’s work on political participation and representation. Through partnerships with parliaments, parliamentary networks, practitioners and other stakeholders, the Institute seeks to strengthen parliamentary capacity and independence while promoting more effective, representative and accountable parliamentary institutions. Its flagship parliamentary strengthening portfolio, Inter Pares, funded by the European Union, supports these efforts by working with parliaments around the world to strengthen their capacity and independence. The Principal Adviser, Parliamentary Strengthening serves as International IDEA’s most senior expert in this field, providing intellectual leadership, setting the strategic direction and safeguarding the quality of the organisation’s parliamentary strengthening work. The role serves as the principal point of contact for Regional Programmes, partners and donors, and identifies strategic opportunities for engagement, including at the intersection of parliamentary strengthening and International IDEA’s broader thematic areas. Duties and Responsibilities Intellectual leadership for Inter Pares. Provides expert substantive guidance for the Inter Pares portfolio as its senior adviser, keeping the work substantively strong and coherent; New opportunities and partnerships. Identifies and develops new opportunities for International IDEA to engage meaningfully on parliamentary strengthening, including where it connects with the organization's other areas of work, such as elections, political finance, gender equality, constitution building, climate change and democratic resilience; cultivates strategic partnerships and positions International IDEA to secure new funding and programme opportunities; Resource mobilization and donor engagement. Leads and supports resource mobilization efforts by identifying funding opportunities, engaging with existing and prospective donors, and contributing to fundraising strategies that advance parliamentary strengthening priorities; Portfolio development. Sets and safeguards the quality standard for parliamentary strengthening work across GP. Provides substantive guidance in the design and development of new project proposals; Support to regions. Supports International IDEA's regional and country teams with expertise on parliamentary strengthening, so their work is well-grounded and consistent; Partner network. Maintains and strengthens International IDEA's network of parliamentary partners, practitioners, and expert institutions; Contribution to collective leadership. Contributes to shared decisions and direction across International IDEA’s Global Programmes as a member of the Global Programmes Leadership Team; General Profile A recognised expert in parliamentary strengthening, with a strong professional reputation, publications, and standing in relevant expert networks; Able to set the direction and safeguard the quality of complex, multi-country work, and to guide the teams that deliver it without directly managing them; A credible, trusted representative of the organization with donors and partners, and in public and policy settings, with a strong understanding of the priorities, structures and ways of working of the European Union as the programme's principal donor; Excellent communicator - in writing and in person - able to engage effectively with a wide range of institutional audiences and to build and sustain collaborative relationships across organizational boundaries; Strong strategic judgement, with the ability to spot and develop new opportunities and partnerships, and to act on them proactively; Acts in accordance with International IDEA’ s core values; Respect, Integrity and Professionalism; Integrates gender equality, diversity, and social inclusion (GEDSI) considerations into all tasks and activities, in alignment with the Institute’s Core Values and commitment to the GEDSI policy. Willing to travel, approximately 25% of the time Reporting line Director, Global Programmes Education and Experience Advanced university degree in political science, international relations, law, development studies, or a related field; A minimum 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in democracy support, governance, political participation and representation, parliamentary strengthening, or a closely related field, including substantial experience working on parliamentary development and democratic institutions; Demonstrated experience providing senior-level substantive advice and technical expertise on parliamentary strengthening, democratic governance, political representation, or related areas, preferably in an international or multi-country context; Proven experience cultivating and managing relationships with bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, development partners, parliamentary institutions and other key stakeholders; Demonstrated experience in the design, development and implementation of complex programmes or projects, including experience working across countries, regions and institutional contexts; Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across organizational units and thematic areas, including providing advice and expertise to Regional and Country Programmes and identifying connections between parliamentary strengthening and other areas of democratic governance; Excellent command of English; knowledge of another International IDEA working language (French, Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese or Russian) is an asset. Terms of Contract: International Post Fixed term appointment for two (2) years . Remuneration - EUR 7 258 NET per month + benefits Applying for this position: Applications should be submitted no later than 23:59 (CEST) 18 October 2026. Please note that all applications must be made in English. Selection Process: Evaluation of qualified candidates will include an assessment and up to two (2) interviews. Candidates selected to proceed to the next stage of the process will be contacted once all applications have been carefully reviewed. All candidates will be notified of the status of their application via email once the process has been finalized Use of AI in Recruitment International IDEA places strong emphasis on human input in recruitment. Candidates must disclose any use of AI tools. All application materials, written assessments, and interview responses (as applicable) must be entirely human-generated and reflect the candidate’s own knowledge, skills, and experience. The use of AI to generate content or misrepresent qualifications is not permitted. AI‑powered assistive technologies (such as screen readers or speech‑to‑text tools) may be used for accessibility purposes to ensure equal access to the recruitment process International IDEA is an equal opportunity employer which seeks to further diversify its staff in terms of gender, culture and nationality

item.title: 2027 Secretary-General’s Office Spring Internship
item.description: Context International IDEA is an intergovernmental organization (IGO) with 35 Member States and an explicit mandate to support sustainable democracy worldwide. International IDEA develops evidence-based knowledge on democracy and supports the implementation of that knowledge in country- and region-specific projects. The Institute is the only IGO solely dedicated to supporting democracy worldwide with permanent UN Observer status. The Institute leverages its unique role as a democracy IGO to convene multilateral and national actors, democracy defenders and civil society to engage in collective global action to champion, defend and advance democracy around the world. The Secretary-General's Office is looking for two interns for spring 2027. The Secretary-General’s Office is an agile and collaborative team that supports strategic leadership, governance, partnerships, and external engagement of International IDEA. Internship Activities The interns will be based at the Secretary-General Office (SGO) and support the SGO in developing relations with Member States and other key stakeholders, strengthening institutional fundraising, and increasing International IDEA’s visibility. The internship is a chance to gain valuable experience in working with democracy, external relations, and diplomacy in an intergovernmental setting. There is regular exposure to and the opportunity to learn from the most senior leaders in the organization, as well as regular interaction with diplomats and politicians in Sweden and around the world. More specifically, the interns, under the guidance of the mentors and other staff members of the SGO, will be responsible for supporting the governance aspects of the Institute including organization of Council of Member State meetings and Board of Advisor meetings, conducting desk research on topics related to democracy, democracy support and development policy, including compiling and drafting materials to support the Secretary-General’s international travels and missions. The interns will also draft communications materials for the SGO, International IDEA website, the internal communications platform, and social media channels. The interns will work with the SGO to develop and strengthen relations with Member States and partner organizations, assist with the preparation of internal and external meetings and events, and assist with minute-taking, logistical support, and follow-up on the contacts established by the SGO. The interns will proactively take part in external events about democracy and related topics and report the key findings to the SGO. The interns will also liaise with peer organizations to seek entry points for engagement with International IDEA. The interns will work closely with event management and help with the coordination of events such as registration, outreach, and other logistics. The interns will support outreach and communication with the Stockholm-based diplomatic community and work with the SGO’s External Relations team to support resource mobilization efforts with Member States and other donors. This includes exposure to and participation in planning and fundraising meetings with senior leaders and donors. Additionally, the interns will support the SGO’s reporting to Member States, donors, and other stakeholders and perform other tasks as assigned. Management and Organization The interns will have a dedicated mentor within the Secretary-General’s Office team. Given the internship tasks, the intern is expected to be in person in Stockholm, Sweden. The interns will work at least 3 days per week in the office and can work remotely 2 days/week (the interns can also choose to come into the office all 5 days/week). Timing and Working Plan The internship position will be full-time from 25 January 2027 to 4 June 2027 (or as agreed with the mentor). The interns will work office hours from 09:00 – 17:00 hrs, if not otherwise agreed with the mentor. Please note that the internship at International IDEA is a full-time position that cannot be combined with other full-time duties such as an academic programme. Students will, however, receive academic credit if the internship is done as part of their programme. The interns will get reimbursed for their transportation card. Qualifications and Required Skills For this internship, we are looking for two students enrolled in a programme or recent graduates focusing on social science; political science; international relations; human rights; law; development studies or a related field. The ideal candidate possesses: Excellent knowledge of written and oral English; Passion and high motivation for working with democracy and international affairs; Strong communications and writing skills, and an ability (or willingness to learn) to formulate and summarize complex issues in an accessible way; Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including good judgment and ability to proactively seek guidance and assistance where required; Good organizational, prioritization, and coordination skills. Ability to balance event management and logistical tasks from different team members; Ability to assess, manage and structure information; Ability to appreciate diversity and work in a high diversity work environment; Good interpersonal and cooperation skills, including willingness to accept diverse tasks and ability to prioritize according to importance and urgency; Knowledge of Microsoft Office package. Meritorious skills/experience: Experience working, studying and/or volunteering in an international context is considered an advantage; Knowledge of Swedish, Spanish and/or French would be an asset. Selection Process Applications should be submitted no later than 23:59 (CET) 01 November 2026. Candidates selected to proceed to the next stage of the process will be contacted once all applications have been carefully reviewed. Evaluation of shortlisted candidates will include an interview and if needed, a short-written test/assessment. All candidates will be notified of the status of their application via email once the process has been finalized. Terms of internship This is internship is unpaid , and insurance cover in respect of travel, health, medical costs, disability, accident, and death is not provided by International IDEA. It would be your responsibility to make your own insurance arrangements to ensure such cover. This position is open to those legally authorized to live and work in Sweden for the duration of the internship. International IDEA is not able to support work permit applications or relocation costs. Learn more about International IDEA. International IDEA is an equal-opportunity employer which seeks to further diversify its staff in terms of gender, culture and nationality.
